A1.justification: Both complete, readable 14-page PDFs describe the same DiffDIS research. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original DIS5K benchmark results, component and denoising ablations, and qualitative segmentation comparisons in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged, including one-step denoising, joint mask/edge prediction, batch-discriminative embeddings, DBIA, and scale-wise conditional injection.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DIS5K training, validation, and four test subsets. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 11 baselines, including GenPercept, MVANet, and BiRefNet. The qualitative comparison and DBIA interaction comparison also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains identical splits, five metrics, 1024×1024 inputs, training settings, and evaluation binarization. The denoising configurations and DIS-VD ablation protocol are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The VAE reconstruction analysis, edge/DBIA visualization, component ablations, pretrained-weight and denoising-step comparisons, and interaction ablation remain identical in Tables 1 and 3–5 and Figure 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 2 reports DiffDIS DIS-VD maximum F-measure of 0.908 and MAE of 0.029 in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including the one-step denoising derivation, training objective, and mutual attention formulation, are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about segmentation accuracy, rapid one-step inference, detail preservation, and improved determinism.

C2.justification: Interpretations of edge-assisted determinism, SD-Turbo initialization, and multi-step stochasticity are unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, optimization settings, and preprocessing instructions are identical. Both retain the same future code-release statement and repository hyperlink.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, and the complete reference list are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to segmentation and diffusion research.

P1.justification: v3 adds the running text 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Body wording, terminology, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The added publication header and updated first-page margin stamp make small visual changes. Figures 1–6, Tables 1–5, captions, placement, and body layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revisions identify conference publication and update version markings. Scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and body presentation are identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
